text:
Week 36 of building in public. 🇹🇴
My family and I are building an app to teach my teenagers Tongan — and through it, our culture. Just us, no company.
Where we're at: 200+ downloads, 64 subscribers, 8K+ views on our launch post. 🙏
Two honest updates: on launch day Apple missed approving our subscriptions for a few hours, so I opened the whole app for free until they fixed it — if things felt off, that's why. And I said Android would be live this week. I was wrong — Google's review needs 1–2 more weeks. That's on me.
This week: getting Android approved and recording the last of the audio myself.
Follow along to watch a family try to keep a language alive. 👇 On Android? Drop a 🤖. Speak Tongan? Drop a 🇹🇴.

#buildinpublic #tongan #tonga #languagelearning #indiehacker

text:
Nobody enrolled. Zero signups. And I'm saying it out loud because that's what building in public actually means.

The program is good, I know because I'm running it one-on-one in parallel right now. The gap wasn't in what we built. It was in how we got it in front of the right people.

That's a completely different problem. With a completely different solution.

Visibility isn't just showing up online. It's being findable where people are already looking. And the Business Visibility Blueprint just gave me my biggest lesson in business visibility.

Every learning is a data point.
